subject: Post-demo: quantify streaming concurrency & egress hop budget
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: FinixCloud DevOps <infra@finixcloud.com>
Date: 2027-03-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: quantify streaming concurrency & egress hop budget

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the data points we need to properly size a private/VPC inference rollout for your streaming use case.

Recap (what we heard from FinixCloud):
- Primary requirement: real-time streaming completions for user sessions (websocket-like) with per-session p95 latency target <= 120ms for ~512-token responses (typical chunked at 64 tokens).
- Sustained concurrency expected: ~200 concurrent streaming sessions; allowed burst up to ~800 for ~30s during traffic spikes.
- Throughput: rough estimate today is ~10K tokens/sec aggregate during peak, but you said you can provide exact numbers.
- Networking: your infra sits in GCP us-central1, currently NAT egress to partner transit, and a Cloud VPN to the partner edge.

Asks / action items for sizing and validation:
1) Please send a traceroute / mtr from your app-hosts (us-central1) to the Redwood egress IPs (I listed our egress IPs in the HubSpot note; I can re-send) and one tcpdump/pcap capturing a streaming session (SNI + TLS handshake + first 2 chunks).
2) Confirm observed egress bandwidth (Gbps) and whether you have 10Gbps links available for direct peering/VPC attachment.
3) Any firewall / IDS appliances that rewrite TCP options, terminate TLS, or apply SYN-rate limiting? These commonly impact streaming keepalive behavior.
4) Your desired data residency (region) and whether you require private peering (BGP) vs site-to-site VPN.
5) Confirm MTU (do you run jumbo frames inside the VPC?) and any expected packet shaping.

I've attached the demo recording and included a short checklist below we use for preflight network validation. If you can send the traceroute + pcap by EOD tomorrow we will run a lab run against a staging VPC and give you an estimated GPU count and latency budget.

Quick checklist for you to confirm (we'll validate):
- Traceroute/MTR to Redwood egress IPs
- TCP dump of a representative streaming session (first 2 chunks)
- Egress bandwidth (observed and provisioned)
- MTU / firewall middleboxes / TLS offload
- Expected concurrency profile (sustained vs burst) and token distribution

Next steps: after we get the traces we'll run them through our network model and return a latency budget + a recommended initial deployment (model variant, quantization, GPUs, and autoscale knobs).

Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (video/mp4)

Thanks — talk soon.

Karthik — thanks for the summary and the checklist. Couple of quick answers from infra:

Environment notes:
- Primary region: GCP us-central1 (we have failover in us-east4).
- Current egress: NAT Gateway to partner transit, measured sustained egress ~8 Gbps, with occasional bursts to 11 Gbps.
- VPN: Cloud VPN to partner edge, median internal latency ~50ms to your partner POP, jitter ~5ms.
- MTU: 1460 across the path (no jumbo frames).
- Firewall/IDS: we have an inline IDS that performs TLS metadata extraction (SNI only), does not terminate TLS. No TCP option rewriting that we're aware of, but we can confirm.

Concurrency/traffic:
- Our real-time websocket service currently holds ~400 concurrent websocket connections per region for normal traffic; we would prefer not to exceed 400 steady but can burst to 800 for short periods.
- Token distribution: typical response sizes center around 350-700 tokens; chunk at ~64 tokens if the model supports streaming.

Attachments (we're sending these now):
- network-diagram.pdf (high-level topology showing where the Cloud VPN and partner transit sit)
- capture-session.pcap (sample tcpdump capturing a short real streaming session)

We can also stand up a short maintenance window if you want us to run an MTR/traceroute simultaneously to capture live paths. If you send the list of Redwood egress IPs again I'll run traceroute and a pcap and return them by EOD.

Regards,

Karthik / Marissa — reviewed the pcap and diagram. Short technical readout below; happy to flesh out a doc for FinixCloud.

Quick latency budget (p95 estimate for a 512-token streaming response, 64-token chunks):
- App -> customer edge (LB) : ~10-15ms (internal to their VPC)
- Customer edge -> egress NAT / partner transit: ~15-20ms (observed path + NAT)
- Internet/transit between partner POP and Redwood ingress: ~18-25ms (depends on peering)
- Redwood ingress + TLS handshake + routing: ~12-15ms
- Model inference (quantized Llama-2-13B, chunked streaming, optimized kernels): ~35-45ms (p95)

Estimated p95 total (sum): ~90-120ms. With direct peering (BGP) we expect the transit leg to drop by ~8-12ms, pushing p95 comfortably below 110ms. So, yes — meeting <= 120ms is feasible given their numbers and with peering recommended.

GPU sizing / throughput guidance (streaming):
- Baseline performance (our lab numbers, quantized 13B): ~2,500 tokens/sec per A10x-equivalent GPU under continuous streaming load (64-token chunks).
- For 200 steady concurrent sessions averaging 500 tokens each and assuming interleaved chunked streaming, the token/sec requirement is roughly: 200 sessions * (500 tokens / avg session duration) — conservative estimate ~8-10K tokens/sec aggregate.
- At 2.5K tokens/sec per GPU, plan for 4 GPUs to handle steady load with headroom.
- For bursts to 800 conc for 30s, autoscale to 6 GPUs (fast scale) or use reserved burst capacity; suggest 2-3 extra GPUs as buffer and quick scale policy to add 2 GPUs per 60s while streaming to minimize cold-starts.

Other mitigations / recommendations:
- Enable prefix/KV caching for any repeated prompts to cut token work.
- Prefer model variant with int8/4 quantization for lower inference time; we can run quality tests during the lab.
- Offload TLS termination to their LB if they can (keeps TCP handshake cost local); if not, peering helps reduce handshake RTT.
- Ensure TCP window scaling is enabled and keepalives are >= 30s to avoid idle timeouts.
- MTU 1460 is fine; ensure no PMTU blackhole on the transit path.

Next steps (for the reply to Elena):
1) We ask FinixCloud to run a simultaneous traceroute + tcpdump during a short 15-min window (we'll provide Redwood egress IPs and a staging endpoint) so we can correlate latencies.
2) Share the pcap and traceroute results; we'll run a lab replay and return: (a) measured p95 under identical load, (b) GPU count recommendation, (c) suggested autoscale policy and model variant.
3) If they prefer, we can propose a short pilot with BGP peering (1-2 week) to measure real-world improvements.

I'll attach our egress IP list and a short network preflight checklist for them.
